Subject: Re: Privatelisting: escrow & invoicing for Azure Private Plan

Thanks — good questions. Quick answers up front, followed by proposed next steps: 

1) Escrow/holdback: For Azure Private Listings we typically recommend using Azure's merchant invoicing with a seller-level settlement holdback configured. That means Azure will settle to Redwood but we can configure a 30-day holdback on the seller payout. If Bluestone requires the funds held by a third-party escrow, we can discuss an addendum but that is uncommon and will require payment flow wiring work.

2) Invoice routing & PO: There are two common patterns: (a) Azure issues invoices on behalf of the marketplace (invoice shows Azure as biller with merchant settlement details in settlement file) or (b) Redwood issues invoices directly to the customer and reconciles with Azure settlements. For procurement workflows we usually recommend (a) because it avoids duplicate invoices and maps cleanly into Azure's PO fields (merchant ID, PO number).

Next steps I propose: 
- We attach the commercial_summary_v1.pdf (included) for the SOW.
- I’ll loop in Legal (Irene) to confirm any redline necessary for the payment routing language.
- I’ll reach out to Azure contacts to confirm the specific invoice field mapping for merchant ID + PO.

If Bluestone prefers Redwood to invoice directly, we can do that; it will require an invoice routing SLT in the contract (timing for settlements differs). Which billing entity should appear on your PO?

Best,

Karthik / Procurement team — adding a quick legal note.

We reviewed the standard Private Listing billing exhibit. A couple items to flag for Bluestone to confirm: 

- Holdback mechanics: our preference is to use Azure merchant holdback (seller settlement delay) rather than Redwood-managed escrow. That keeps funds and tax handling with the marketplace. If Bluestone insists on a creditor-controlled escrow, we need a short addendum to specify escrow agent, trigger conditions for release, and an indemnity carve-out for allocation of chargebacks.

- Invoice entity: If Azure invoices on our behalf we must include language that Azure settlements are the accounting event that triggers Redwood revenue recognition; if Redwood invoices directly we need a payment routing SLA and refund/countercharge clause in the SOW.

I've attached a marked copy with two alternative clauses (A: Azure merchant invoicing; B: Redwood invoicing and routing SLA). Please review and let us know which you prefer so we can finalize the SOW.

Hi all — cc’ing to clarify Azure marketplace-side options so procurement has what they need: 

- Merchant settlement holdback: Azure can configure holdback windows (e.g., 30 days) at the publisher/merchant level for Private Offers. The holdback is applied in the settlement file and reflected in merchant payouts.
- Invoice presentation: Azure can issue invoices on behalf of the marketplace with custom fields (PO, merchant ID). Those invoices are what customers receive; Redwood will receive settlement files that include line-level merchant identifiers.
- Delegated billing: If Redwood wants to invoice directly we can enable delegated billing but that requires a seller onboarding step and changes to settlement cadence (and delays tax reconciliation).

Attached is a short guide outlining invoice fields and sample settlement CSV. If you want, I can have the marketplace onboarding engineer join a 30-minute call to walk Bluestone’s AP team through the fields they need to validate their PO parser.

Cheers,
